children: CoreWeave (CRWV, Financials) is set to receive $350 million in computing-related spending from the charitable foundation established by former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori, according to recent tax disclosures.
The Jen-Hsun & Lori Huang Foundation's last filing revealed the promise. A June Nvidia filing named CoreWeave as the receiver and indicated $108.3 million spent.
The funding supports the Computing Initiative for Open Science, which gives researchers access to large-scale GPU computing resources.
The foundation does not directly use computing power, CoreWeave claimed. Scientific research grant awardees receive the resources.
Investors are scrutinizing AI infrastructure firms' financial interactions with consumers. For its cloud computing company, CoreWeave relies on powerful GPUs. Nvidia is a key stakeholder.
This is the Huang Foundation's greatest 2025 donation. Almost three times its 2024 donations, the organization gave $373 million last year.
At Dec. 31, 2025, its assets were $12.7 billion, up from $9.2 billion. About 90% of the assets were Nvidia shares.
The foundation gave the California College of the Arts $19 million and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology $1.2 million.
CoreWeave investors see the pledge as more computing service demand, but it also shows how the AI infrastructure sector is financially intertwined.
Investors will scrutinize future disclosures for CoreWeave's remaining computing obligations and revenue contribution.

title: Jensen Huang's $350 Million CoreWeave Deal Raises Questions About AI Financing
